messages.content: I just realized @asic destroyer KianV will boot linux for around 5 to $10 most of the cost is connectors
@asic destroyer on your TT910 - SPI is for storage, but where is the ram?
@urish 🖕🏻
@carlfk - The SPI pmod has both spiflash and psram (spi sram)
is that the ram that the cpu uses to run linux?
@carlfk - That is my understanding
OpenRam on the die?
@carlfk - Where did OpenRAM on the die come from? I just said psram on the SPI pmod?
I mean could that be an option for a future die?
No - Linux needs megabytes of memory -- which is not possible on a 180nm process node.
ah shucks.   was wondering how low we could drive the price.
@carlfk - I'm pretty sure that the final cost for any wafer.space Linux capable device is going to be around $100 USD based on a roughly $30 USD BOM.
@carlfk

@carlfk, that is why I implemented the SDRAM controller for GF180MCU. I need memory. The only memory I need on the chip is for the caches. I implemented those in GF180 as well. You can see all the SRAM cells around my design.
how much cache did you create?
I$: 4Kib, D$: 2 Kib
21 SRAM-Tiles

I used them here

https://gf180mcu-pdk.readthedocs.io/en/latest/IPs/SRAM/gf180mcu_fd_ip_sram/cells/gf180mcu_fd_ip_sram__sram512x8m8wm1/gf180mcu_fd_ip_sram__sram512x8m8wm1.html
Crazy Caches
@carlfk  FYI, my new quad-core RISC-V SoC uses 224 KiB of cache memory for L1 and L2.
at the show last weekend people were asking me stuff like "how much can you fit?"  so 224k is now an answer I can give them :p
Currently, my 325T Kintex-7 SoC is packed with stuff

@carlfk Just to give you an idea: if you built a Kintex 7 325T as a GF180 FPGA, the die would be something like 55 × 55 to 90 × 90 mm. That is a rough estimate based on scaling the 28 nm FPGA fabric to the 180 nm GF180MCU process.
thats a big die :p
@carlfk - I have numbers on the website now
Not quite a Kintex 7 325T -- but if you have ever wondered what the Artix 7 15T die looks like -> https://siliconprawn.org/archive/doku.php?id=azonenberg:xilinx:xc7a15t
